uncertain.text: vu tel coffre quand ie parti: ce que fut
uncertain.note: sic, wrong sort: the word is 'vn' (un tel coffre) but the print sets 'vu'. At 12x with contrast (body-7.jpg, and again on foot.jpg) the second letter has two separate top serifs with clean white between them and the connecting stroke at the foot, exactly like the u of 'quand' four words later; the n of 'quand', of 'dans' on the line above and of 'vn' at blocks[2].lines[10] and lines[14] all show a solid arch springing from the top of the left stem. Transcribed as printed. The reconciler should confirm on the full-resolution scan.

key 'o': the note's leading letter is a fully closed oval with a visible counter (margin-1.jpg, 14x, normalized), unlike the open italic c of 'au c.' and 'c. per tuas.' in the two notes above it. There is NO marker {o} anywhere in the body of this page, and the printer's alphabet would give c after the page's a and b, so this is most likely a wrong sort for a key 'c' whose marker is also missing (or which belongs to the run continuing on the next page). Recorded as printed with the key 'o'; the missing marker for key o is what this entry documents.

uncertain.text: ſouuient-il pas quand nous eſtions à vn
uncertain.note: the print sets 'eſtionsà' with no gap (body-4.jpg, 4x): 'eſtions' and 'à' are distinct words, so one space is set between them per §1 word division. Same normalization applied at 'les chauſſes' (lines[20], printed 'le s chauſſes' with the gap inside the word) and 'bles de' (lines[22], printed 'blesde').

uncertain.text: ne ſoit fils de Pierre, ou q̃ Frãçois ſoit fils de Ieã, ou au
uncertain.note: the marks over q, over the a of 'Frãçois' and over the final a of 'Ieã' are all the same flat, slightly wavy bar with hooked ends (6x, body-2.jpg), not the steep short wedge of the acute at 'difficulté' and 'arriué'; read as nasal tildes (que, François, Iean). Same bar over 'cõme' (lines[3]), 'filiatiõ' and 'biẽ' (lines[5]).

'præterea' carries a true æ ligature (9x). Two marks follow the final a: a round point on the baseline and a smaller point raised above it. Read as a period plus an ink speck; a colon is the alternative. Also in this note: 'veniens . i.&' is set with a space before the period and none after 'i.', normalized per §1 to 'veniens. i. &'.

the third letter is a plain e carrying a flat bar, not an æ ligature (compare the unmistakable æ of 'præterea' in note a); read as the nasal tilde, quẽ = quem, which with 'aper,' on the next line gives the Digest title 'quemadmodum testamenta aperiantur' (D. 29.3). 'quæ' is the alternative reading. 'teſt.' uses the italic curled-top t of §2.

'ij' is the italic ÿ-shaped ij sort, transcribed decomposed as on p058. 'P.' is an italic capital P with no stroke through the stem and no descender, standing where the citation wants the paragraph sign §; transcribed as printed, following the same decision on p058 ('P rogo', 'l. ſi cui. P.'). 'ſi' is long ſ + i, which in this italic looks like an fi ligature.

page furniture: running head 'PARLEMENT DE THOLOSE.' and the TEXTE heading are both set in spaced capitals, closed up per §3 with spaced_caps true; folio '63' at the top right, matching the manifest. No signature, no catchword, no ornament and no foot citation block — foot.jpg and body-8.jpg are blank below the last body line, and margin-2/3/4.jpg carry no notes (all three notes sit at the head of the margin). Punctuation spacing normalized throughout per §1 (the print sets 'perplex:eſquels', 'paſſées:& di', 'propos:meſmes', 'parti : ce' and commas tight or with a space before).
